paragraphs.title: The Feast and the Desecration of the Temple Vessels

easy.explanation: Belshazzar the king made the great feast.
Belshazzar made a feast to a thousand of his lords.
easy.q: How many of his lords attended the feast?

answers: The golden and silver vessels from the temple
easy.explanation: They drank from the vessels taken out of the temple in Jerusalem.
easy.q: What did Belshazzar and his guests drink from?

answers: That the temple vessels be brought
medium.explanation: Belshazzar commanded that the golden and silver vessels be brought.
medium.q: What did Belshazzar command while he tasted the wine?

medium.explanation: Nebuchadnezzar had taken them from the temple in Jerusalem.
medium.q: Where had the vessels been taken from?

answers: The gods of gold, silver, brass, iron, wood, and stone
medium.explanation: They praised the gods made of various metals, wood, and stone.
medium.q: What did the people praise after drinking from the vessels?

answers: Sacred temple vessels were used to honor lifeless idols
The king drank water instead of wine
The nobles refused to attend the feast
challenge.explanation: The holy vessels were used in a feast where lifeless idols were praised.
challenge.q: What contrast is emphasized in this scene?

answers: He planned to return them to Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: Using the temple vessels for a pagan feast showed contempt for their sacred purpose.
challenge.q: What does Belshazzar’s use of the vessels reveal about him?

answers: Gold, silver, brass, iron, wood, and stone
challenge.explanation: The verse lists gold, silver, brass, iron, wood, and stone.
challenge.q: Which materials are specifically named as belonging to the gods they praised?

paragraphs.title: The Writing Hand and the King’s Terror

easy.explanation: The fingers of a man’s hand appeared and wrote on the wall.
easy.q: What appeared suddenly during the feast?

answers: On the plaster of the palace wall
easy.explanation: The hand wrote upon the plaster of the wall of the king’s palace.

answers: He was greatly troubled and afraid
easy.explanation: The king’s countenance changed and his thoughts troubled him.

medium.explanation: The king called the wise men of Babylon to read and interpret it.
medium.q: Whom did the king summon to read the writing?

answers: Scarlet clothing, a gold chain, and the position of third ruler
medium.explanation: The king promised clothing, a gold chain, and the third position in the kingdom.
medium.q: What reward did the king offer to whoever interpreted the writing?

answers: Read the writing or make known its interpretation
medium.explanation: They could not read the writing or explain its meaning.
medium.q: What were the wise men unable to do?

answers: They could not read or interpret the writing
They did not know where the feast was held
challenge.explanation: The wise men came, but they could neither read nor interpret the writing.
challenge.q: What was the immediate problem faced by Babylon’s wise men?

answers: His lords were astonished and confused
challenge.explanation: The king was troubled, and his lords were astonished.
challenge.q: How did the king’s fear affect those around him?

answers: He saw the source of the message but could not understand it
He saw it only after falling asleep
challenge.explanation: The king saw the part of the hand that wrote, yet still needed an interpreter.
challenge.q: What is significant about the king seeing the hand itself?

paragraphs.title: The Queen’s Advice and Daniel Is Summoned

easy.explanation: The queen came into the banquet house and recommended Daniel.

answers: An excellent spirit, knowledge, and understanding
easy.explanation: She said Daniel had an excellent spirit, knowledge, and understanding.
easy.q: What qualities did the queen say were found in Daniel?

answers: The king could keep them and give the rewards to another
easy.explanation: Daniel told the king to keep his gifts and give the rewards to another.
easy.q: What did Daniel say about the king’s gifts?

answers: Because of his ability to interpret difficult matters
Because he was a member of the royal family
medium.explanation: Daniel was known for interpreting dreams, hard sentences, and doubts.
medium.q: Why did the queen recommend Daniel?

answers: Read the writing and make known its interpretation
medium.explanation: The king asked Daniel to read and interpret the writing.
medium.q: What did Belshazzar ask Daniel to do?

answers: Scarlet clothing, a gold chain, and the position of third ruler
medium.explanation: Belshazzar repeated the promised reward of clothing, a chain, and royal rank.
medium.q: What did the king promise Daniel if he could interpret the writing?

answers: He valued declaring the truth above personal gain
He was afraid to speak to the king
challenge.explanation: Daniel agreed to interpret the message without seeking the king’s reward.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Daniel’s refusal of the gifts?

answers: The queen recommends Daniel, Daniel is brought in, and the king asks for the interpretation
Daniel interprets the writing, then the queen recommends him
The king leaves, and Daniel refuses to enter
challenge.explanation: The queen recommends Daniel, he is brought before the king, and the king questions him.
challenge.q: Which sequence of events occurs in this passage?

answers: He is presented as able to explain what they could not
He is unable to read the writing
He refuses to appear before the king
challenge.explanation: The wise men failed, but Daniel was called because he could make the interpretation known.
challenge.q: How is Daniel contrasted with the wise men of Babylon?

easy.explanation: Daniel began by speaking of Nebuchadnezzar, Belshazzar’s father.
easy.q: Whom did Daniel discuss at the beginning of his speech?

answers: He was deposed from his throne and lost his glory
easy.explanation: He was deposed from his kingly throne and his glory was taken from him.
easy.q: What happened to Nebuchadnezzar when his heart was lifted up?

easy.explanation: Daniel said Belshazzar had not humbled his heart.
easy.q: What did Daniel say Belshazzar had failed to do?

answers: That the most high God rules in the kingdom of men
That kings should hold longer feasts
That temple vessels should be hidden
medium.explanation: Nebuchadnezzar learned that the most high God rules over human kingdoms.
medium.q: What lesson should Belshazzar have learned from Nebuchadnezzar?

answers: Belshazzar praised the God of heaven
Belshazzar drank from the temple vessels and praised idols
Belshazzar gave Daniel a royal position
medium.explanation: Belshazzar drank from the holy vessels and praised gods of metal, wood, and stone.
medium.q: Which action repeated the sin of the feast?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes pride and self-exaltation.
medium.q: What does the phrase “his heart was lifted up” mean in context?

answers: Belshazzar knew what had happened to Nebuchadnezzar but still refused to humble himself
Belshazzar had never heard of Nebuchadnezzar
Nebuchadnezzar asked Belshazzar to interpret the writing
challenge.explanation: Belshazzar knew the lesson of Nebuchadnezzar’s humiliation but did not respond humbly.
challenge.q: What is the connection between Nebuchadnezzar’s story and Daniel’s rebuke of Belshazzar?

answers: Because Belshazzar had not glorified God, whose hand held his breath and ways
Because the wise men requested it
challenge.explanation: Belshazzar praised idols instead of glorifying the God who held his life and ways.
challenge.q: Why was the writing sent, according to Daniel?

answers: The most high God rules in the kingdom of men
The wise men hold ultimate authority
challenge.explanation: Daniel states that the most high God rules in the kingdom of men.
challenge.q: What central truth about human kingdoms does Daniel emphasize?

easy.explanation: Those four words were written on the wall.
easy.q: What words were written on the wall?

answers: Belshazzar was weighed and found wanting
easy.explanation: TEKEL meant that Belshazzar was weighed in the balances and found wanting.

answers: He became ruler of another kingdom
easy.explanation: Belshazzar the king was slain that night.
easy.q: What happened to Belshazzar that night?

answers: God had numbered Belshazzar’s kingdom and finished it
The king had received a new kingdom
The people had chosen a new ruler
medium.explanation: MENE meant that God had numbered the kingdom and brought it to an end.

answers: The kingdom would remain with Belshazzar
The kingdom would be divided and given to the Medes and Persians
The kingdom would be given to Daniel
medium.explanation: PERES meant that the kingdom would be divided and given to the Medes and Persians.
Belshazzar was weighed and found lacking.

answers: The kingdom is numbered and finished, the king is found wanting, and the kingdom is divided
The kingdom is divided, then numbered, and finally found complete
The kingdom grows, the king becomes wealthy, and the writing disappears
challenge.explanation: The meanings progress from MENE to TEKEL to PERES.
challenge.q: What is the logical order of the interpretation?

answers: Belshazzar honors Daniel, but is slain that same night
Daniel is punished, but Belshazzar escapes
Belshazzar interprets the writing, but Daniel remains silent
challenge.explanation: Belshazzar rewarded Daniel, yet he was slain that very night.
challenge.q: What contrast appears at the end of the story?

answers: It was only a distant warning
The judgment followed immediately after the message
The writing had nothing to do with the king
challenge.explanation: Belshazzar’s death that same night immediately fulfilled the message about the end of his kingdom.
challenge.q: What does the timing of Belshazzar’s death show about the interpretation?
